title: State Machine Orchestration of an HPC Workflow in Cloud
problem: Porting HPC workflows between cloud and on-premises environments is non-trivial; existing designs may not efficiently leverage cloud-native orchestration frameworks.
motivation: Uncertain HPC resource availability drives need for portable workflows; Kubernetes offers advanced orchestration but HPC workflows weren't designed around cloud-native patterns.
method: They took MuMMI, an ensemble workflow (a coordinated set of computational tasks), and redesigned it to run on Kubernetes, a cloud platform for managing containerized software. The redesign transformed it from traditional HPC (where tasks run tightly coupled on a supercomputer) to a cloud-native architecture where components can be independently deployed and scaled. They tested two coordination methods: service-based orchestration that uses shared filesystems to pass data between tasks, and event-driven orchestration where each completed task sends a message to trigger the next step.
key_novelty: Event-driven orchestration—where completed tasks automatically trigger the next step via messages—achieves better performance and lower cloud costs for HPC workflows compared to service-based coordination.
contributions: Event-driven orchestration design for MuMMI on Kubernetes
62.24% faster CPU workflow; 40.29% faster GPU workflow completion
45.0% CPU cost reduction; 38.3% GPU cost reduction
primary_theme: Cloud-native HPC workflow orchestration via event-driven design
